subject: Fewest silver
claim: Every player sits at 0 silver at round end, so the contest becomes an all-way tie that pays everyone the same.
evidence: All four held 0 at the end of rounds II and III, each getting 3 then 5 (32 followers that separated nobody), while 101 of 224 decisions reasoned about it.

subject: Fewest silver
claim: Choosing to pay with silver first quietly wins a share of Fewest silver, which makes routine payments a small decision.
evidence: At least 9 payments were made silver-first to reach 0 (e.g. Ava's 10-follower buy at [225], Dee's at [188]), and Dee caught a suggested payment that would have cost her a 5-follower share.

subject: Fewest silver
claim: Silver given to rivals during a round is always spent or converted before scoring, so only a round-end gift moves the contest.
evidence: 33 silver was gifted during rounds (Toast, Party Gifts, Largesse) and every recipient was back at 0 by scoring; only Kingmakers' round-end gift ever broke a tie.

subject: Party Gifts
claim: Giving silver with Party Gifts or Toast works as a weapon that breaks rivals' zero-silver ties.
evidence: None of the 6 in-round gifts broke a tie; Cal's round I gift of 3 silver to Ben became part of Ben's Guest of Honor payment after Polish.

subject: Largesse
claim: Largesse is +10 followers plus a split of 12 silver that hands rivals spending money rather than hurting them.
evidence: Ben took +10; Ava spent 6 of her 8 gifted silver on the Double Agent that took Ben's Guest of Honor, and all three recipients were at 0 silver by scoring.

subject: Largesse
claim: Who gets Largesse is a turn-order lottery.
evidence: Ben had the fewest followers after round II (37), so he placed first in round III and took Largesse before anyone else could; Dee placed third.

subject: Fewest members
claim: A player who holds zero members takes Fewest members every round and nobody can contest it.
evidence: Dee won 18 from it and finished last on 83; Ava pushed a member onto her with Guest of Honor at [171] and Dee answered with Write-Off.

subject: Fewest members
claim: Holding nothing is a real plan: Modest Means, Catch Up and Fewest members all pay a lean cult.
evidence: Dee took Modest Means +5 twice, Catch Up +6, and Fewest members +6 and +10, buying 43 followers, the most at the table.

subject: Anchorites
claim: Anchorites pays +5 every round end for almost no cost to a small cult.
evidence: It paid Cal 15 plus 1 printed for 6 resources, bought on his first placement, the best return of any card (also 15 in pilot3).

subject: Anchorites
claim: No member-taking card can reach Anchorites.
evidence: Swindle took it at [92] and Mutineers took it back at [125]; Ava passed it over with both Double Agent and Poach.

subject: Kidnappers
claim: Because the victim chooses which member to give, Kidnappers only ever collects a rival's used-up card.
evidence: It cost 10 and a recruit and returned about 3 followers; Cal gave the spent Mutineers both times.

subject: Most resources
claim: Holding the resource lead pulls against recruiting, so the leader skims 1-follower buys or passes.
evidence: Ava passed one recruit and made two or three 1-follower buys to hold it; it paid her 4 + 6 + 5 = 15.

subject: Most resources
claim: Deciding how much to spend while staying ahead of rivals' best reachable totals is a satisfying decision.
evidence: It was decided by one resource in round I and by a tie at 4 on the last placement of the game, a 10-point swing.

subject: White Cloak
claim: The White Cloak fires so often that the first picker barely has a choice.
evidence: It fired 10 times for 20 white, against 14 magenta, 12 yellow and 8 silver for the other cloaks, and its owner won.

subject: Silver Cloak
claim: The Silver Cloak refunds silver, which works against Silver's Fewest silver contest.
evidence: It was picked last and paid the least (8 silver); the clash cost Dee one round I share (2 followers), and she tied the contest in rounds II and III.

subject: Kingmakers
claim: Kingmakers' round-end gift can break a rival's zero-silver tie with no answer, since it comes after the last placement.
evidence: Its 3 silver to Cal at round I's end turned Cal's solo +4 into nothing; it was the only silver gift all game that changed a contest.

subject: Kingmakers
claim: Being hit by Kingmakers after zeroing your silver feels helpless.
evidence: It cost Cal 4 in round I and nothing after; Cal says his plan leaned on Fewest silver.

subject: Guest of Honor
claim: Guest of Honor gives too much for a 5-cost round I card.
evidence: It was used twice in the whole game (8 followers across two owners) because it needs a member you can spare; Ben left it unused in rounds II and III.

subject: Snitch
claim: Giving Snitch to the rival you steal from turns it against you.
evidence: Ben gave it away for +4 and it then cost him 5 followers through his own Shoplifter skims and Swindle.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: So many cards take members that building a cult makes you a target.
evidence: 7 members were taken (Swindle 2, Kidnappers 2, Mutineers, Double Agent, Poach), but most were junk, Anchorites came back the same round, and Cal, hit 4 times, won.

subject: Write-Off
claim: Write-Off and Farewell pay a member's full cost even after its once-per-game power is spent.
evidence: Talent Scouts (8) gave Ben a free 7-cost member and then 9 white; Ben Farewelled a used Double Agent for 10; Dee Write-Offed a dumped Mutineers for 7 white.

subject: Farewell
claim: Farewell gives an exhausted card one last big payout, which makes spent cards still matter.
evidence: Farewell paid Ben 10 (Double Agent) and Dee 6 (Kingmakers).

subject: Buying followers
claim: Late recruits often come down to a 1-follower buy or a pass.
evidence: 13 of 35 follower buys were 1-follower buys and 2 recruits were passed; only with the White Cloak did a 1-follower buy feel worth it (it returned 2 white).

subject: Buying followers
claim: The 1, 5 and 10 sizes turn the last placements into arithmetic about landing on exactly 5 or 10.
evidence: Ben's and Dee's final placements were chosen to make exactly 5; Ava's final 5-follower buy left her 4, tied by Cal's cloak refund, which decided first place.

subject: White Cloak
claim: A rival's cloak trigger is easy to forget when sizing a final margin.
evidence: Ava left 4 resources at [239] counting Cal's best as 3; his cloak refund made it 4 and turned her +10 into +5 each, a 10-point swing in a 4-point loss; Dee had spotted the same threat at [241].

subject: Help Yourself
claim: Help Yourself grows with every minion you've placed, so taking it late is strong and leaving it open is a risk.
evidence: On Ava's fourth round III minion it stole 4 and emptied both Cal and Dee, turning Dee's planned 5-follower buy into a 1-follower buy.

subject: Help Yourself
claim: One steal breaks a lean player's planned finish.
evidence: It cost Dee 4 followers because she held exactly the 2 resources she needed, as she says herself.

subject: Catch Up
claim: Catch Up pays a player who just spent everything, a built-in catch-up.
evidence: It paid 7, 6 and 6 resources in its three uses.

subject: Polish
claim: Polish flips a losing silver position into a tie and funds a member of another color in one placement.
evidence: Used 3 times, each to reach 0 silver; Ben's round I Polish paid for Guest of Honor.

subject: New Blood
claim: New Blood with the Yellow Cloak refunds most of a new-color member.
evidence: Twice it plus the cloak returned 5 yellow on a new-color recruit, fully refunding Early Traders.

subject: Early Traders
claim: Early Traders' round-start swap makes resource colors almost meaningless for its owner.
evidence: Ben swapped 4 and then 2 resources at round starts to fit each next buy exactly.

subject: Modest Means
claim: Modest Means pays the player with the fewest members, which fits a lean plan.
evidence: +5 white in all three uses.

subject: Splurge
claim: Splurge's round II rate turns a member purchase into as many followers as it costs.
evidence: Cal's two-turn Makeover-Splurge chain paid +6 on Mutineers, which then took Anchorites back (about a 20-point swing against Ben).

subject: Swindle
claim: Swindle can rip a key member from the leader and hand back a dead card, a big late swing.
evidence: Round II it took Cal's Anchorites (recovered); round III it took Ava's Dabblers, cutting her Yellow from solo +10 to a +5 share each.

subject: Swindle
claim: Swindle counts as a recruit (Shoplifter, Yellow Cloak) and as a steal (Snitch), which its words don't say.
evidence: One Swindle at [227] fired the Yellow Cloak, a Shoplifter skim and Snitch twice, costing Ben 2 followers where he counted 1.

subject: Double Agent
claim: Double Agent hits a rival's engine and moves a contest in one card, but leaves a 10-cost card in the rival's cult.
evidence: Ava paid 10 for Guest of Honor (+4, 1 printed) and Ben Farewelled the Double Agent for 10.

subject: Poach
claim: Poach in round III's center swings a +10 contest both ways at once.
evidence: Poach took Cal's Talent Scouts and gave Ava a fourth member color until Ben's Swindle cut it to three.

subject: Consolation Prize
claim: Consolation Prize keeps lost contests worth something.
evidence: +4 at two round ends = 8, plus 1 printed, for 7.

subject: Cheerleaders
claim: Cheerleaders adds +2 to each contest win, shared ones included.
evidence: Four shared wins paid Ben 8 plus 1 printed; it came free through Talent Scouts.

subject: Cash In
claim: Cash In not using a recruit makes ordering it against follower buys a small puzzle.
evidence: It paid only 3, since Cal had already spent his white on follower buys.

subject: Toast
claim: Toast turns into a weapon in round III because rivals' gifted silver breaks their zero-silver tie.
evidence: All three rivals were back at 0 by scoring after Dee's round III Toast; its real value was 6 silver for Dee.

subject: Dabblers
claim: Dabblers adds a member color, two printed followers and lets you dump silver in one buy.
evidence: It gave Ava a second color in round I (+2 Yellow share) and 2 printed until Ben Swindled it.

subject: Dabblers
claim: Dabblers counts as one extra color in Most member colors but as every color for Melting Pot, and its text says neither.
evidence: The contest counted Ava at 2 colors in round II while Melting Pot paid her for 4 at [84]: +4 followers and 4 resources instead of 2 and 2.

subject: Shoplifter
claim: Shoplifter's skim is forced onto whoever holds resources, even a rival whose Snitch punishes it.
evidence: 11 skims (7 from Cal, 4 from Ava); the 4 from Ava cost Ben 4 followers, three of them forced because Cal and Dee were empty.

subject: Flaunt
claim: Flaunt is never taken because it needs silver in hand at a table where everyone holds 0.
evidence: 0 of 48 placements; every other space except Buyout was taken at least once.

subject: Buyout
claim: Buyout is never taken because it pays in silver and gives +1 silver, which loses Fewest silver.
evidence: 0 of 48 placements; players named it only as a space to avoid ([234], [244]).

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Giving a member to a rival usually helps them, because bodies hurt only the Fewest members leader and Write-Off and Farewell turn a body into its cost.
evidence: 6 of the 7 members given or swapped into a rival's cult helped the receiver (e.g. Talent Scouts gave Cal a Yellow tie, Double Agent gave Ben a Farewell for 10).

subject: Recruiting members
claim: Round III's member shop is ignored because a late member is worth only its printed follower.
evidence: 1 of 8 round III members was bought; 19 of the 20 round III recruits were follower buys.

subject: Recruiting members
claim: A close game was won by a 2-member cult; the 0-member cult was last and the 8-member cult second.
evidence: Final 91, 87, 86, 83; 38% of followers bought, 28% from contests.
